Implemented the admin route with Next.js auth interrupts. [`app/admin/page.tsx`](/vercel/sandbox/app/admin/page.tsx#L1) now reads the session and uses `unauthorized()` when no session exists, then `forbidden()` when the session exists but `role !== 'admin'`, so `/admin` returns framework-managed `401` or `403` responses as appropriate. [`next.config.ts`](/vercel/sandbox/next.config.ts#L1) enables `experimental.authInterrupts`.

The custom boundary UIs are in [`app/forbidden.tsx`](/vercel/sandbox/app/forbidden.tsx#L1) for the 403 page and [`app/unauthorized.tsx`](/vercel/sandbox/app/unauthorized.tsx#L1) for the 401 page. Session lookup is request-scoped in [`app/lib/auth.ts`](/vercel/sandbox/app/lib/auth.ts#L1) via the `session` cookie, parsed as JSON with `userId`, `name`, and `role`.

`npm run build` passes, and `/admin` is now a dynamic route.
